structure.title: Preface
structure.summary: This is a formal notice from Jio Financial Services Limited dated August 5, 2025, addressed to BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited. The company is informing the stock exchanges that the Annual Report for the financial year 2024-25 and the Notice convening the Second Annual General Meeting (Post Listing) are being sent electronically to members with registered email addresses. The notice provides the web links to access the Notice and Annual Report on the company's website. Additionally, it mentions that a letter with the web-link to the Annual Report is being sent to members who have not registered their email addresses, in compliance with SEBI Regulation 36(1)(b). The notice includes the company's contact details, CIN, and is signed by Mohana V, Group Company Secretary and Compliance Officer. Copies are marked to KFin Technologies Limited, Central Depository Services (India) Limited, and National Securities Depository Limited.

structure.title: Jio Financial Services Limited
structure.summary: The notice announces Jio Financial Services Limited's Second Annual General Meeting (post-listing) on August 28, 2025, via video conferencing. Ordinary business includes adopting audited financial statements for FY 2024-25 with Board and Auditor reports, declaring a ₹0.50 dividend per equity share, and appointing Ms. Isha M. Ambani as a Director retiring by rotation. Special business covers appointing S. N. Ananthasubramanian & Co. as Secretarial Auditor for five years and issuing up to 50 crore warrants to promoter group entities on a preferential basis, with detailed terms. AGM notes explain VC/OAVM participation, electronic Annual Report dispatch, director re-appointment, remote e-voting and Insta Poll procedures, login instructions, and scrutinizer details.

nodes.summary: This document is a notice for the Second Annual General Meeting (Post Listing) of Jio Financial Services Limited, scheduled for August 28, 2025, via video conferencing. It includes the company's registered office details and contact information. The notice covers ordinary business items: adoption of audited financial statements (standalone and consolidated) for FY ended March 31, 2025, along with Board and Auditor reports; declaration of a dividend of ₹0.50 per equity share for FY 2024-25; and appointment of Ms. Isha M. Ambani as a Director retiring by rotation. Resolutions for each item are proposed as Ordinary Resolutions.

nodes.title: SPECIAL BUSINESS
nodes.summary: This section on Special Business covers two AGM agenda items: appointment of S. N. Ananthasubramanian & Co. as Secretarial Auditor for five years via Ordinary Resolution, and issuance of up to 50 crore warrants to promoter group entities (Sikka Ports & Terminals Ltd and Jamnagar Utilities and Power Pvt Ltd) on a preferential basis via Special Resolution, detailing terms such as pricing, payment schedule, conversion window, lock-in, and board authorizations. It outlines requirements for updating bank details, PAN, contact information, and specimen signatures. It explains Tax Deductible at Source (TDS)/withholding tax rates for resident and non-resident members, including documents needed for lower or nil tax deduction, such as Form 15G/15H, tax residency certificates, and lower tax deduction certificates. It covers submission deadlines, consequences of non-compliance, issuance of TDS certificates, and indemnification for inaccurate information. Members are advised to consult tax advisors.

structure.title: Access Progress Now
structure.summary: The text is the annual report FY 2024-25 of Jio Financial Services Limited (JFSL), themed 'Access Progress Now,' emphasizing digital-first financial empowerment. It introduces JFSL as a Core Investment Company with subsidiaries (Jio Credit, Jio Insurance Broking, Jio Payment Solutions, Jio Leasing, Jio Finance Platform, Jio Payments Bank) and a joint venture with BlackRock. The report covers company history, listing details, and the JioFinance app offering loans, savings, UPI, insurance, and financial tools. It also contains forward-looking statements and mentions AI-generated images and links to BRSR and ESG reports.

structure.title: About Jio Financial Services Limited (JFSL)
structure.summary: Jio Financial Services Limited (JFSL) is introduced as a digital-first financial services company focused on holistic financial well-being for Indians, using customer-centricity, technology, and data intelligence to offer seamless, affordable, intuitive products. It leverages a vast ecosystem, trusted brand, SaaS-based tech architecture, and institutional partnerships to build a future-ready platform, democratizing access to create scale impact and simplify financial services. The text includes JFSL's vision of empowering every Indian with simple, secure, seamless, smart digital solutions and its mission to be a leading digital-first institution creating sustainable stakeholder value guided by 4R principles: Reputation Above All, Regulatory Adherence, Return on Capital, and Return of Capital. It also references the Annual Report FY 2024-25.

structure.title: JFSL Strategy: Borrow, Invest, and Transact Offerings Overview
structure.summary: The page outlines JFSL's strategy across Borrow, Invest, and Transact. Borrow covers Jio Credit Limited's secured lending products like home loans, loan against property, mutual funds, shares, and corporate/supply chain finance. Invest details joint ventures with BlackRock for asset management, wealth management, and broking, plus Jio Gold digital gold and the 'My Money' personal finance manager. Transact describes Jio Payment Solutions Limited and Jio Payments Bank Limited offering savings accounts, UPI, bill payments, money transfers, and merchant solutions like QR codes, POS devices, payment gateways, UPI International, Jio VoiceBox, and JioSoundPay.

structure.title: Return on Capital
structure.summary: The text outlines Jio Financial Services' goal to deliver consistent returns on capital through scalable platforms, technology, optimized unit economics, risk management, and efficient cost-to-income ratio while promoting inclusive financial access. It presents FY25 performance metrics including total income, PPOP, EPS, AUM, PAT, net worth, employees, and retail shareholders. Key milestones from April 2024 to March 2025 include launching Jio SoundPay, securing an RBI payment aggregator license, SEBI in-principle approval with BlackRock for an AMC, incorporating asset management and trustee companies, JioFinance UPI at Paris Olympics, launching the JioFinance app, hitting 4 million downloads and 8 million monthly active users, JPBL customer base of 2.31 million, strategic group marketing agreement, incorporating Jio BlackRock Investment Advisers, receiving CIC approval, and a JV with BlackRock for wealth management and broking.

structure.title: Chairman's Message on Technology-Driven Transformation in Financial Services
structure.summary: The Chairman's message addresses global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties while noting India's projected 6.5% GDP growth in FY26 and its path to a $5 trillion economy, driven by consumption, policy reforms, talent, and technology. It highlights the financial services sector's transformation through digital platforms and fintech, emphasizing agility and resilience. AI, especially Agentic AI, is presented as a key enabler for personalized advice, back-office automation, fraud detection, and greater financial access and affordability. The message stresses trust, customer data privacy, and cybersecurity investments. It outlines Jio Financial Services' commitment to technology as a force for good, its strong FY25 foundation in people, processes, products, and technology, FY26 ambitions, and focus on governance and risk management, closing with gratitude to shareholders.

structure.title: Giving wings to bold aspirations
structure.summary: A letter to shareholders from Isha M. Ambani, Director, highlighting Jio Financial Services Limited's FY25 progress: scaling distribution platforms, expanding product offerings, and deepening customer engagement. It states the vision of accessible, personal, empowering finance for all Indians regardless of geography or background, and the mission to provide simple, trusted, intelligent solutions via digital innovation like the JioFinance app. It notes millions of users and the first dividend payout, reinforcing long-term shareholder value. Looking ahead, JFSL aims to play a pivotal role in India's financial evolution by listening to customers, adapting with agility, and serving with integrity to deliver lasting value.

structure.title: Scaling with purpose. Leading with discipline.
structure.summary: The letter to shareholders from Jio Financial Services Limited (JFSL) highlights its technology-centric approach, FY25 as a pivotal year with strong execution and growth, and its future-ready tech stack using data analytics and AI. It details the JioFinance app's 4 million downloads, expanded distribution through MyJio and 14,000+ Business Correspondents, and business performance: Jio Credit Limited's AUM growth to ₹10,053 crore, Jio Payments Bank's 2.31 million customers and ₹295 crore deposits, Jio Payment Solutions' new licence and innovations, Jio Insurance Broking's ₹900 crore premium from 1.81 million policies, and the JioBlackRock JV's progress. It covers the team of over 1,000 professionals, financial results (total income ₹2,079 crore, PAT ₹1,613 crore, dividend of ₹0.50 per share), ₹1,346 crore equity infusion, and risk-calibrated growth with strong governance, concluding with gratitude and mission.

structure.title: Group Structure
structure.summary: The text outlines Jio Financial Services Limited's group structure, listing entities with ownership percentages and regulatory details: Jio Credit Limited (NBFC), Jio Leasing Services Limited, Reliance International Leasing IFSC Private Limited (JV), Jio Insurance Broking Limited, Jio Payment Solutions Limited, Jio Payments Bank Limited (with SBI stake acquisition), Jio Finance Platform and Service Limited, Reliance Industrial Investments and Holdings Limited, and Jio BlackRock JVs in investment advisory, broking, asset management, and trusteeship. It identifies JFSL as the Core Investment Company and holding company. The text also introduces the Annual Report theme 'Access Progress Now' and JFSL's growth strategy based on four tenets: customer delight, best for India, technology and data analytics, and responsible growth with governance and sustainability.

structure.title: JioFinance App Customer Delight
structure.summary: The text highlights the JioFinance app's customer-centric vision, emphasizing clarity, ease of access, and trust. It introduces Jio Finance Platform and Service Limited (JFPSL) as the digital-first strategy anchor, managing the unified JioFinance app for borrowing, transacting, investing, and protecting. A customer testimonial praises digital gold investing. Key metrics include 8 million+ monthly active users and 4 million+ app downloads as of March 2025. The value proposition covers one-view financial control, new-age products, strong brand, robust security, AI-driven insights via 'My Money' module, and seamless digital journeys. Key highlights include integration with MyJio, user growth, My Money launch, global UPI launch during Paris Olympics 2024, product expansion, and AI-powered personalization.

structure.title: Our Businesses
structure.summary: The text highlights JFSL's diverse financial services businesses. Jio Credit Limited provides digital-first retail and corporate lending with ₹10,053 crore AUM, expanded to 10 Tier-I cities, and launched digital lending journeys. Jio Payments Bank offers digital banking with 2.3 million accounts, ₹295 crore deposits, 14,000+ BC points, and 1 million+ UPI users. Jio Payment Solutions provides omnichannel payment solutions, secured RBI Payment Aggregator Licence, and launched JioSoundPay and VoiceBox. Jio Insurance Broking facilitated ₹900 crore premiums, 1.81 million policies, expanded D2C platform and embedded insurance. JioBlackRock joint venture received SEBI approvals for AMC, wealth management, and broking, leveraging BlackRock's Aladdin platform for digital-first investment access.

structure.title: Leveraging Technology
structure.summary: The text highlights technology as central to delivering financial access at scale and cost points suited to Indian customers. It emphasizes creating tailored user journeys, reducing friction, and offering secure, responsive services through intelligent systems built for scale, speed, and personalisation. A modular, scalable technology stack and data intelligence engine enable reaching the right customer with the right product, at the right time, and through the right channel.

structure.title: CORE PHILOSOPHY
structure.summary: The text outlines JFSL's Technology function core philosophy, emphasizing agility, standardisation, and intelligence. It details seven principles: fit-for-purpose architecture, experience-driven design, embedded AI, real-time insights, operational excellence, cost efficiency, and reliability. It describes the data and infrastructure layers, including data sources, advanced analytics, governance, and AI infrastructure, highlighting cybersecurity and privacy. Strategic outcomes include precise targeting, improved customer experience, early warning signals, and operational efficiencies. The intelligence layer covers predictive analytics, AI agents, business intelligence, and hyper-personalisation. Key highlights include JioFinance app 2.0, Enterprise Data Lake, SaaS and AI-driven shared services, AI for customer queries, continuous monitoring, enhanced security, customer experience enhancement, operational efficiency, innovation in lending, unified customer identity, and platform architecture with 24/7 security operations and AI-driven insights.

structure.title: Growing Responsibly
structure.summary: The text outlines Jio Financial Services Limited's 'Growing Responsibly' approach to creating long-term value through strong governance, ethical conduct, and sustainability. It details a comprehensive strategy built on four pillars: a robust enterprise-wide Risk Management framework, regulatory adherence, investment in people for a future-ready workforce, and commitment to ESG principles. The Risk Management section describes its core philosophy, governance structure, risk categories managed (credit, market, liquidity, operational, outsourcing, strategic, fraud, model, digital), alignment with the 4Rs (Reputation, Regulation, Return on Capital, Return of Capital), automation, monitoring, and business continuity. Key FY25 highlights include comprehensive risk coverage, proactive identification, mitigation frameworks, technology adoption, business continuity planning, strategic integration, and enhancing the 4Rs.

structure.title: JFSL Risk Management: Resilience, Governance, and Key FY25 Highlights
structure.summary: The page outlines JFSL's Risk Management philosophy, emphasizing a strategic, enterprise-wide framework aligned with risk appetite and governance roles. It lists managed risk categories (credit, market, liquidity, operational, outsourcing, strategic, fraud, model, digital) and alignment with the 4Rs (Reputation, Regulation, Return on Capital, Return of Capital). Key sections cover Automation of routine calculations, Monitoring systems for emerging risks, and Business Continuity with tiered recovery plans and RTOs. FY25 highlights include comprehensive risk coverage, proactive identification via self-evaluation and analytics, mitigation frameworks with dashboards and Board-approved policies, technology adoption, robust BCP/DR, strategic integration into investment and lending, and contribution to the 4Rs.

structure.title: Fostering a culture of adherence
structure.summary: The text outlines Jio Financial Services Limited's Compliance function and HR strategy. Compliance is built on regulatory integrity, zero tolerance, and a group-wide framework for adherence. Key highlights include a unified compliance tool for centralized monitoring, guidance notes for consistency, an AI-powered AML and transaction monitoring tool, transition to an NBFC-CIC structure, and embedding compliance via KPI-linked 'Regulations'. HR strategy focuses on a digital-first, future-ready workforce with three pillars: Capability (talent acquisition, upskilling, leadership), Culture (high-performance, inclusive environment), and Collaboration (cross-functional partnerships), underpinned by employee well-being, diversity, and digital transformation.

structure.title: KE Y HIGHLIGHTS
structure.summary: The text highlights JFSL's FY25 achievements in talent acquisition, employer branding, global expertise, diversity, agile talent models, leadership development, digital transformation, technological innovation, employee engagement, and strategic talent deployment. It also covers ESG governance, financial inclusion, nation-building, social responsibility, climate change, and CSR initiatives, including financial literacy, digital inclusion, healthcare, education, and rural development, along with key metrics such as employee strength, CSR spend, and diversity indicators.

structure.title: JFSL FY25 ESG & CSR: Sustainability Governance and Four Strategic Objectives
structure.summary: JFSL outlines its ESG governance framework, led by a board-level ESG committee, and its four sustainability objectives. Financial Inclusion covers financial literacy camps, digital inclusion, savings accounts, non-metro store growth, chatbot languages, and CSR spending. Nation-building focuses on financing underserved segments and MSMEs to drive economic development. Social Responsibility details diversity and inclusion, mandatory ESG training, value chain partner engagement with NGRBC and BRSR, Supplier Code adherence, and CSR programs via Reliance Foundation in rural development, education, healthcare, and culture. Climate Change covers monitoring and disclosing GHG emissions, energy, water, and waste to set reduction targets.

structure.title: Financial empowerment through digital access
structure.summary: JFSL's FY 2024-25 annual report highlights financial empowerment through digital access, structured around four sustainability pillars: Financial Inclusion, Social Responsibility, Climate Change, and Nation Building. It details services like Lend & Lease, Invest, Transact, and Protect, alongside initiatives such as phygital banking, digital lending, UPI, POS, and investments for MSMEs and underbanked communities. Social responsibility covers accessible credit, employment generation, employee development, and ethical sourcing. Nation-building efforts include tax contributions, digital service adoption, and entrepreneurship support aligned with Digital India and Atmanirbhar Bharat. Climate action focuses on green financing for solar panels and energy-efficient solutions. The report also presents key metrics: 646% customer increase, 22.4 lakh active users, ₹17.7 crore CSR spend, 100% POSH training, 25% female workforce, 1:1.17 compensation ratio, and ₹334.32 crore in taxes.

structure.title: Committed to powering a sustainable future
structure.summary: JFSL integrates climate action into its sustainability strategy, guided by its ESG Policy, focusing on energy and emissions management, waste reduction, sustainable procurement, renewable energy, paperless processes, and responsible resource consumption, with specific metrics on energy use, Scope 2 emissions, water used, waste generated, and single-use plastics avoided, plus green tariffs in Mumbai avoiding CO2 emissions. Social responsibility covers employee well-being, inclusion, and community development, with data on professionals onboarded, business correspondent network expansion, gender pay parity, women in workforce, and CSR programs reaching people in Odisha and Maharashtra, supported by ₹17.7 crore allocation. Transparency is maintained through BRSR and ESG reports.

structure.summary: The text covers accounting policies for employee benefits, including long-term benefits accrued over service periods, defined contribution plans with fixed payments and no further obligation, defined benefit plans calculated annually using the projected unit credit method with remeasurements in other comprehensive income, and leave encashment determined actuarially and discounted. It also details earnings per share calculations for basic and diluted shares, foreign currency transaction and translation rules for monetary and non-monetary items, operating segment reporting aligned with internal reporting to the CODM, and contract liabilities recognized when consideration is received before goods or services are transferred.

structure.title: D. Critical accounting judgements and key sources of estimations uncertainty
key_items: D.1 Provisions and contingent liabilities; D.2 Impairment of financial assets; D.3 Fair value measurement; D.4 Defined benefit plans (gratuity benefits); D.5 Income Taxes
structure.summary: This text discusses critical accounting judgements and estimation uncertainties, covering management's use of estimates and assumptions that affect reported amounts, with actual results potentially differing. It outlines five specific areas: D.1 Provisions and contingent liabilities, requiring judgement for recognition, quantification, and estimating resource flows; D.2 Impairment of financial assets, involving judgement in measuring impairment losses, estimating future cash flows, and assessing credit risk increases; D.3 Fair value measurement, using valuation techniques like DCF and judgement for unquoted financial instruments, including inputs like liquidity risk, credit risk, and volatility; D.4 Defined benefit plans (gratuity benefits), determined via actuarial valuations with assumptions on discount rate, inflation, salary increments, and mortality rates; and D.5 Income Taxes, regarding the availability of future tax profit against which tax losses carried forward can be used. All estimates are reviewed regularly.

structure.title: E. Recent accounting pronouncements
structure.summary: The text covers recent accounting pronouncements from the MCA, including Ind AS 117 and amendments to Ind AS 116, effective April 1, 2024, with no impact on financial statements. It then presents notes to the consolidated financial statements: cash and cash equivalents, bank balances, and trade receivables. For trade receivables, it provides details on amounts, impairment loss allowance, and ageing schedules for 2025 and 2024, including undisputed and disputed receivables, with no amounts due from directors or related parties.

structure.title: 4 Loans
structure.summary: The section covers financial statement notes on loans, including gross and net amounts, impairment allowances, security details, loans to related parties, finance lease receivables, credit quality stages, and impairment charges. It also details investments: joint ventures (equity and preference shares in JPBL, RILIPL, and Jio BlackRock entities), associates (Reliance Services & Holdings, Petroleum Trust), and others by measurement category—at cost (settlors contribution), at fair value through OCI (equity shares, preferred shares, units), at fair value through profit or loss (equity shares, commercial paper, certificates of deposit, treasury bills, mutual funds), and at amortised cost (government securities, bonds, TREPs). Additionally, it covers other financial assets, current and deferred tax assets/liabilities, property, plant and equipment, capital work-in-progress, intangible assets, goodwill, other non-financial assets, and payables.

nodes.title: 4 Loans (intro)
nodes.summary: The text presents detailed financial statement notes on loans, including gross and net loan amounts at amortised cost, impairment loss allowances, and security details (secured vs. unsecured). It covers loans to promoters, directors, KMPs, and related parties, finance lease receivables with maturity analysis, and credit quality exposure by stage (1, 2, 3) with movements in impairment allowances. It also details impairment charges in profit and loss, investments accounted under the equity method, other investments by category (mutual funds, government securities, TREPs, etc.), and disclosures on investments in India and outside India, including a note on proposed acquisition of Jio Payments Bank shares.

nodes.title: A.1 Investment in Joint Ventures

It lists investments in Jio Payments Bank Limited (JPBL), Reliance International Leasing IFSC Private Limited (RILIPL), Jio BlackRock Investment Advisers Private Limited (JBIAPL), Jio BlackRock Asset Management Private Limited (JBAMPL), and Jio BlackRock Trustee Private Limited (JBTPL). For each entity, it provides the number of shares, face value (₹10 each), investment amounts (in crores), and percentage holdings. Additionally, it includes a preference share investment in RILIPL. nodes.title: A.2 Investment in Associates
nodes.summary: The text presents notes to consolidated financial statements, detailing investments in associates (equity and preference shares of Reliance Services & Holdings Limited, and Petroleum Trust corpus), investments in others (settlors contribution, equity/preferred shares, units, and fair value/amortized cost investments), and category-wise investment breakdown. It also covers other financial assets (receivables, deposits, unbilled revenue), current tax assets, and deferred tax assets/liabilities with reconciliations of charges/credits recognized in profit or loss and other comprehensive income, including tax items under section 43B and fair value adjustments.

nodes.title: B.4 Investments measured at amortised cost
nodes.summary: The text presents notes to the consolidated financial statements of Jio Financial Services Limited for FY 2024-25, covering investments measured at amortised cost (including government securities, bonds, and TREPs), with details on quoted/unquoted investments, market value, and category-wise investments (equity method, cost, amortised cost, FVOCI, FVTPL). It also includes other financial assets (receivables, security deposits, unbilled revenue), current tax assets, deferred tax assets and liabilities with related charge/credit and reversal details, property, plant and equipment with gross block, depreciation, and net block, capital work-in-progress with ageing schedules, intangible assets under development, goodwill, other intangible assets (software), other non-financial assets (balances with government authorities, prepaid expenses, advances), and payables (trade payables including micro and small enterprises).

structure.title: Notes on Fixed Assets, Intangibles, Non-Financial Assets, and Payables
structure.summary: The page presents notes to consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It details property, plant and equipment with gross block, depreciation, and net block for 2025 and 2024, including equipment, office equipment, computers, furniture, and vehicles. Capital work-in-progress and intangible assets under development are shown with ageing schedules. Goodwill movement is provided. Other intangible assets (software) are detailed with gross block, amortisation, and net block for both years. Other non-financial assets include balances with government authorities, prepaid expenses, and other advances. Payables section begins but is incomplete.

It also details income sources (interest, dividend, fees, net gain on fair value changes, other income), expenses (finance costs, impairment, employee benefits, depreciation, other expenses including CSR and auditor payments), tax expenses, earnings per share, segment reporting, a scheme of arrangement involving demerger from Reliance Industries Limited and subsequent share cancellations, and contingent liabilities and commitments.

structure.summary: The text details inputs, assumptions, and estimation techniques for Expected Credit Loss (ECL), including significant increase in credit risk, probability of default, loss given default, exposure at default, forward-looking information, and default definition. It also covers concentration of credit risk with tables of gross carrying amount and ECL by stage. Additionally, it discusses market risk, interest rate risk, liquidity risk with maturity analysis, operational risk, capital management, and maturity analysis for assets and liabilities, providing comparative figures for 2025 and 2024.

structure.title: Credit Risk, Liquidity, Market Risk, Operational Risk and Capital Management

structure.summary: The page covers credit risk assessment, including ECL methodology, definition of default, concentration of credit risk with exposure and ECL tables. It then addresses market risk, interest rate risk, and liquidity risk, including a liquidity analysis for non-derivative financial liabilities. Operational risk management is described, followed by capital management strategies. The page includes tabular data on gross carrying amounts and ECL by stage, and contractual maturity analysis of financial liabilities.

It details financial assets (cash, bank balances, trade receivables, loans, investments, other financial assets) and non-financial assets (current tax assets, deferred tax assets, property, plant and equipment, capital work-in-progress, intangible assets, goodwill, other intangible assets, other non-financial assets). Similarly, it lists financial liabilities (trade payables, debt securities, borrowings, other financial liabilities) and non-financial liabilities (deferred tax liabilities, provisions, other non-financial liabilities), with totals for each category. Additionally, it includes disclosures for employee benefits under Ind AS 19, specifically contributions to provident, superannuation, and pension funds for both years.

structure.title: Defined benefit plan
structure.summary: The text details the defined benefit plan accounting, including the projected unit credit method for present value obligation and recognition of compensated absences. It presents tables reconciling opening and closing balances of defined benefit obligation and fair value of plan assets for gratuity (funded and unfunded) for years ended March 31, 2025 and 2024. It shows amounts recognized in the balance sheet, expenses in profit and loss and other comprehensive income, actuarial assumptions (mortality table, discount rate, salary escalation, turnover), expected contributions for next year, and maturity analysis of projected benefit payments for future years.

structure.title: Sensitivity analysis
structure.summary: The text covers sensitivity analysis of actuarial assumptions (discount rate, salary increase, employee turnover) for defined benefit obligations for 2024-25 and 2023-24, including the projected unit credit method. It also lists categories of investments in plan assets as of March 31, 2025 and 2024. Additionally, it provides related party disclosures under Ind AS 24, including a list of related parties (companies under common control, joint ventures, associates, key managerial personnel), transactions with them (e.g., investments, revenue, expenses, dividends), and balances as of March 31, 2025, with detailed amounts in crore.

structure.title: Related Party Transactions: Loans and Material Transactions Disclosures
structure.summary: The page presents notes to consolidated financial statements for FY2025, detailing loans to companies under common control (Reliance Retail, NowFloats, Reliance Corporate IT Park, Reliance Industries) and material related party transactions with joint ventures, associates, and other related entities. It lists transactions by category: purchase/subscription and sale/redemption of investments; purchase of property, plant, equipment, and intangibles; revenue from operations; dividend received; rent, taxes, and energy costs; distribution of shares received; employee benefits; professional fees; information and technology fees; payment processing charges; selling and distribution expenses; CSR expenses; and general expenses, with corresponding amounts for 2024-25 and 2023-24.

It includes: Note 15 on payment to key managerial personnel for Reliance Retail Limited, Reverie Language Technologies Limited, and Jio Things Limited, detailing relationships, remuneration for 2024-25 and 2023-24, with a note on ordinary course and arm's length transactions. Investment details in Jio BlackRock entities are provided. Note 40 lists subsidiaries consolidated under Ind AS 110 with ownership percentages for 2025 and 2024. Note 41 lists associates and joint ventures under equity method with ownership percentages. Note 42 provides additional information required by Schedule III, including parent's share in net assets, profit or loss, and other comprehensive income.

structure.title: Indian Subsidiaries
structure.summary: The text presents financial data for Indian subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures of Jio Financial Services Limited for FY 2024-25. It includes a table listing subsidiaries with percentage holdings, financial figures (assets, liabilities, income, profit, etc.), and acquisition dates. It also covers notes on long-term contracts (none with material losses), proposed dividends, and other statutory information: no benami property proceedings, outstanding borrowings of ₹3,970 crore, no wilful defaulter status, no transactions with struck-off companies, no fund diversion for ultimate beneficiaries, no unrecorded income, no crypto currency trading, and no revaluation of assets. It mentions a recommended final dividend of ₹0.50 per share and board approval on April 17, 2025. Additionally, it includes details on associates and joint ventures with investment values and shareholding percentages, and notes on reporting periods and subsidiary operations.

structure.title: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements: Long Term Contracts and Other Statutory Information
structure.summary: The page covers notes to the consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2025. It includes a section on Long Term Contracts, stating that the Group had no long term contracts, including derivative contracts, with material foreseeable losses requiring provision. The Other Statutory Information section details: no benami property proceedings; outstanding borrowings of ₹3,970.00 crore secured against current assets (₹Nil at March 31, 2024); not declared a wilful defaulter; no transactions with companies struck off under Section 248; no advances, investments, or loans to intermediaries for ultimate beneficiaries, and no funds received with such understanding; no unrecorded transactions surrendered as income; no trading or investment in crypto or virtual currency; and no revaluation of property, plant and equipment or intangible assets. Additionally, it includes a statement containing salient features of financial statements of subsidiaries/associates/joint ventures as per the Companies Act, 2013, with line items such as holdings, share percentage, dividends, comprehensive income, total income, profit/loss before and after taxation, provision for taxation, investments, and liabilities.

structure.title: Events after reporting date

It notes regrouping/reclassification of previous year figures. It includes Annexure A, Part A: Subsidiaries, listing six subsidiaries with details such as ownership percentage, reserves, assets, liabilities, investments, turnover, profit, net worth, and acquisition dates. Part B: Associates and Joint Ventures, listing seven entities with shareholding, investment amounts, net worth, profit/loss, and consolidation notes. It also includes notes on subsidiaries yet to commence operations, no subsidiaries bought/sold during the year, and changes in holding percentage for Jio Payments Bank Limited.

It includes revenue, other income, expenses, profit/loss, comprehensive income, dividends, contingent liabilities, and commitments. Notes explain trust shareholding and group share references. The document ends with signatures from auditors and board members, dated April 17, 2025.
